pool_referrers.boundary: Whole-case route counter arithmetic and recorded target mapping/source identity only. Counters do not assign route work or elapsed time to individual requests.

native.boundary: Saved target-process mapping inventories are linked to rehashed current bytes. No live-process maps or GPU execution is recreated by this CPU review.

pool_referrers.boundary: Saved target-process provider and mapped-file observations, joined to source and fresh build evidence. Counts cover whole case brackets and do not locate or time request-level scans. The independent API benchmark has no separate provider counter bracket; its build/artifact identity is checked separately.

raw_matrix.boundary: Independent graph-submitted F.linear on every checkpoint layer and BF16 BMM at every compressed-key geometry. CUDA events include graph launch. BMM uses GQA-expanded keys and materializes rectangular scores; causal useful and dense executed FLOPs differ. Excludes attention QK/PV, softmax, selection, compression, normalization, RoPE, activation, cache and host validation. A sum of shape-weighted independent API medians, not an observed full request.

accepted_wall_and_api_comparison.boundary: Wall latency is the accepted uninstrumented runner request including token validation/upload, admission/eviction, required history construction, candidate, and cleanup. Complete API GPU execution-span unions come from a separate exact-output profile: first correlated device activity to last completion per invocation, including intra-API gaps but excluding earlier host work. They are not API CPU/wall latency. Activity-only unions are also retained. Raw F.linear/BMM medians cover the matching GEMM/BMM subset and omit sparse QK/PV and helpers; BMM expands GQA and materializes rectangular scores. Full-model and raw-subset MFUs have different numerators. Their same-subset ratio uses GEMM/BMM FLOPs over full runner wall time. Raw matrix plus profiled attention is only a composition estimate; it does not establish an independent full-model matrix-API baseline or a passed proximity gate.

async_end_to_end_speedup.rule: strictly lower total uninstrumented request latency over the complete trace; visit groups reported separately
async_end_to_end_speedup.boundary: Observed trace comparison; no statistical-confidence or repeatability claim

native_provenance.boundary: All libraries mapped before the independent raw matrix benchmark match the replay's final inventory and retain identical recorded file identities afterward. Newly mapped libraries are classified only as raw-benchmark additions; they are not evidence that replay used those libraries. Native build/dependency identity is unchanged throughout.

All384 layer miss unions, logical bytes, interval slots, integer-nanosecond unions/intersections, and exact per-page stripe min/max envelopes were reconstructed independently.

Existing source-bound timeline/API attribution analyzers were rerun on all24 raw traces. Independent activity unions, root containment, shape-driven scope counts and API/wall denominators were additionally reconstructed.
CPU launch cost is not identified by GPU idle time or before-next-submission gaps alone. Those gaps also include host work, dependencies, synchronization, and profiler effects.
Separate profiled API spans include intra-API device gaps and exclude pre-device host work. They must not replace accepted uninstrumented runner wall latency.
Category unions overlap and are non-additive. Fused attention is not simultaneously counted as independent fetch and math; internal overlap uses softmax-only work in a separate clock domain.
Raw GEMM/BMM covers a matching subset and excludes sparse attention. Raw-plus-profiled attention is an estimate of composed cost, not an observed complete standalone baseline.
Failed overlap and end-to-end speedup gates remain valid negative results. API proximity awaits the independent attention/API reference.
